name: GEORGIA

flag.title: Flag of Georgia
flag.note: White with red cross & four red crosses

lead: Tucked between the Caucasus and Black Sea, Georgia is tiny but extraordinary. People pressed grapes here 8,000 years ago — the world's oldest wine. Its singers harmonise in three independent voices; one Georgian song was even sent into space. Ancient towers, fiery food, and a unique alphabet make this place one-of-a-kind.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Founded c. 458 AD by hot springs

geo: Georgia sits at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, with the snow-capped Greater Caucasus range forming a giant natural wall along the north. Mount Shkhara soars to 5,201 m — taller than anything in the Alps.

The west enjoys a lush, subtropical climate fed by Black Sea breezes, while the east is drier and sunnier. Tbilisi sits in a warm river valley famous for naturally hot sulphur springs that bubble up right in the city.
animals: Georgia's mountains shelter the East Caucasian tur — a wild goat with spectacular curved horns — which scrambles across cliffs at up to 4,000 m. The elusive Caucasian leopard, the world's largest leopard subspecies, still prowls remote forests.

Each autumn, over one million raptors funnel through the Batumi bottleneck on the Black Sea coast — one of Earth's great bird migrations. Ancient Colchic rainforests in the west shelter the endemic Caucasian salamander.
culture: Georgians have made wine for 8,000 years using qvevri — clay jars buried underground. The wine ferments slowly in the cool earth, giving it a golden, nutty character. UNESCO added this ancient method to its heritage list in 2013.

Georgian polyphonic singing — three voices weaving independent melodies — is one of the oldest musical traditions on Earth, also UNESCO-listed. The Georgian alphabet, mkhedruli, dates to the 5th century and is used nowhere else in the world.
history: Ancient western Georgia was Colchis — the very land where Greek hero Jason sailed to steal the Golden Fleece. By the 11th century, a united Georgian Kingdom stretched from the Black Sea to the Caspian in a golden age of art and learning.

Georgia was absorbed into the Russian Empire in the 19th century, then into the Soviet Union in 1921. When the USSR collapsed, Georgia declared independence on 9 April 1991 and has been reclaiming its ancient identity — wine, script and song — ever since.
wows: Georgia is the birthplace of wine: 8,000-year-old grape residue was found in Neolithic villages near Tbilisi.
A Georgian folk song, Chakrulo, was placed on the Voyager Golden Record sent into space in 1977.
The Georgian alphabet has 33 letters and is one of the world's few truly original scripts.
Tbilisi is named after hot springs: a king built it where his falcon's prey fell into steaming waters.
Over one million birds of prey migrate past Batumi on the Black Sea in a single autumn season.
Georgia has over 500 indigenous grape varieties — more than almost any other country on Earth.
Georgia's three ancient scripts are UNESCO heritage: Asomtavruli, Nuskhuri, and Mkhedruli.

myths.myth: Georgia is part of Russia / Eastern Europe
myths.fact: Georgia is in the South Caucasus, not Eastern Europe. Its language, script and culture are entirely its own — most Georgians proudly identify as European.
Georgia is a wine nation. Wine has been central to Georgian life for 8,000 years. The local spirit is chacha, a grape brandy — vodka is not part of the tradition.
